subject: SSO/SCIM/IP orchestration - implementation sequencing & mutual action plan
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Reynolds <olivia@healthly.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Oct 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SSO/SCIM/IP orchestration - implementation sequencing & mutual action plan

Hi Olivia — great to kick this off. Thanks for agreeing to the implementation runbook sync. Attaching a lightweight mutual action plan (Healthly_MutualActionPlan_v1.xlsx) and an example SAML metadata file to speed the IdP handoff.

High-level sequencing I recommend for the first 2 weeks:
- Day 0–2: Exchange SAML metadata + test IdP connect (SP-initiated).
- Day 3–5: SCIM provisioning smoke tests (create/update/delete) against staging.
- Day 6–8: IP allowlist confirmation and service-account provisioning.
- Day 9–14: Cutover window + validation + rollback plan.

Action items for Healthly:
1) Provide IdP metadata (SAML) and sample user/group attribute map (email, name, role claim) — target: EOD Thu (2028-10-04).
2) Confirm SCIM attributes required (custom attributes?) and whether groups map to application roles.
3) Share IP ranges for staging and prod (CIDR or specific egress IPs).

From Redwood side:
- Monica will own SCIM mapping and run provisioning checks.
- Ben will coordinate service-account creation and minimal RBAC for connectors.
- I will draft the cutover checklist and create the SUP ticket for tracking.

Notes / constraints:
- For SCIM, we prefer users identified by immutable externalId + primary email. If you plan to include nested groups or role claims, flag that now — it adds 1–2 days.
- If Healthly requires strict IP allowlisting per role (e.g., admin-only CIDR), that will affect our staging verification cadence.

Next step: 30-minute technical sync tomorrow at 10am PT (I’ll send calendar invite). If that time doesn’t work, propose alternatives.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Olivia Reynolds <olivia@healthly.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@healthly.com
Date: Tue, 03 Oct 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SSO/SCIM/IP orchestration - implementation sequencing & mutual action plan

Thanks Marcus — this looks good. Confirming we’re aligned on the proposed window. I’ve looped in our security team (security@healthly.com). Quick answers:
- We can get IdP (Okta) metadata to you by tomorrow EOD, attaching the preliminary export for reference (will send final via secure channel).
- For SCIM: primary attributes: userName (email), externalId (immutable id), displayName, groups. We also have a custom attribute "department_code" — we can decide whether to sync it at a later stage.
- IP allowlist: staging egress will be 18.205.22.0/24 and production will be 18.205.100.0/24 (we’ll confirm).

Questions for Redwood:
1) For service accounts, do you require a specific naming convention? We prefer "healthly-redwood-<env>-svc".
2) What is Redwood's expected behavior on SCIM deprovision (suspend vs delete)? We generally request soft-delete (suspend) for 30 days.

We’re good for the 10am PT sync — I’ll have our IdP engineer join.

—Olivia
Olivia Reynolds
IT Security Lead, Healthly Systems
olivia@healthly.com

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Oct 2028 12:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: SSO/SCIM/IP orchestration - implementation sequencing & mutual action plan

Adding a few technical notes to prep for tomorrow’s sync — copying content that will be useful to share with Healthly.

SCIM mapping recommendations (staging -> Redwood staging tenant):
- id/externalId: map to Okta immutable id (preferred).
- userName: primary login email (case-normalized).
- active: boolean. On deprovision, set active=false and mark suspended timestamp; we keep a 30-day grace window before hard delete by default. (Olivia: that aligns with your ask.)
- groups: sync list of group names and map to application roles via mapping table. If Healthly wants direct role claims instead of group->role mapping, note that requires additional claim configuration on the IdP side.

Service account guidance: see attached service-account-guidelines.md — recommend naming as Olivia suggested but add a suffix for purpose and rotation schedule, e.g., healthly-redwood-prod-connector-2028-10. Minimum scope: token minting + provisioning webhook invoke. No interactive logins.

IP allowlist: we’ll need the exact egress CIDRs for both staging and prod. On our side, we’ll add allowlists for the connector IPs and for our observability endpoints (read-only). If Healthly plans to restrict admin console access by IP, call that out now — it affects corporate SRE access patterns.

Testing plan for tomorrow’s sync:
- Validate SAML SP-initiated sign-in to staging (IdP cert + metadata).
- Create SCIM user via provisioning API and verify attribute set.
- Add user to a group, verify role mapping.
- Test IP-based access to staging console (if requested).

I’ll bring the SCIM curl examples and sample mapping file to the meeting.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai

Attachment: service-account-guidelines.md (md)

Thanks everyone — solid sync today. Quick recap + agreed next steps (I’ve also opened SUP-2314 to track tasks):

Agreed deliverables and owners:
- Healthly: final IdP metadata (Okta) + attribute map — owner: Olivia — due: 2028-10-04 EOD (received preliminary).
- Redwood (Monica): prepare SCIM mapping file and run provisioning smoke tests against staging — due: 2028-10-06.
- Redwood (Ben): create service accounts in prod and staging with naming convention "healthly-redwood-<env>-svc" and set rotation policy — due: 2028-10-05.
- Joint: confirm staging/prod CIDRs and update allowlists — due: 2028-10-05.

Cutover window proposed: 2028-10-11 03:00–07:00 PT (low activity). Rolling back will re-enable old provisioning and detach SCIM in <30m if needed.

Open items:
- Olivia — confirm whether department_code needs to be synced this phase (if yes, we add 1 day).
- Security — any documentation requirements for audit logs (retention, export format)? If so, we’ll include in the plan.

I’ll attach the SUP ticket and the mutual action plan to the Jira linked in the related links. If there are no blockers, we’ll run the staging smoke tests next week and schedule a dry run before cutover.

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround.
